goal: Arduino Uno LED dimmer: a 10k potentiometer (outer legs to 5V and GND, wiper to A0) sets the brightness of a yellow 5 mm LED on PWM pin D9 through a 220 ohm resistor.

plan.title: Arduino Uno Yellow LED Dimmer with Potentiometer
plan.summary: This project creates an adjustable LED dimmer using an Arduino Uno. By turning a 10k potentiometer, the Arduino reads an analog voltage signal and changes the brightness of a yellow LED using pulse-width modulation (PWM).
plan.final_result: When powered by the USB cable, rotating the potentiometer knob smoothly adjusts the yellow LED from completely off to full brightness using hardware PWM.
safety: Always disconnect the USB cable before inserting or moving components on the breadboard.
Never connect the LED directly between 5V and ground without the 220 ohm resistor, or it will burn out immediately.
Ensure the outer legs of the potentiometer do not short together directly into 5V and GND on the same row.

parts.name: Arduino Uno Rev3
parts.why: Controls the circuit by reading the knob angle on analog input A0 and outputting a dimming signal to the LED on digital pin 9.

parts.name: Breadboard, full size (830 tie points)
parts.why: Provides solderless connection points to mount the LED, resistor, potentiometer, and wire everything together.

parts.name: 5 mm yellow LED
parts.why: Lights up and changes brightness according to how far you turn the potentiometer.

parts.name: 220 ohm resistor (yellow LED)
parts.why: Limits electrical current through the LED so it does not burn out.

parts.name: Potentiometer 10 kΩ (rotary, 16 mm)
parts.why: Acts as a rotary dial to supply a variable control voltage between 0 and 5 volts.

parts.name: Jumper wires
parts.why: Carry power, ground, and data signals between the Arduino Uno and the breadboard.

part_guide.bb1: A white plastic grid block with internal spring clips that lets you connect wires and electronic parts without soldering.
part_guide.uno: The main microcontroller board that reads the analog potentiometer voltage and generates the PWM dimming signal for the LED.
part_guide.led_yellow: A yellow 5 mm light-emitting diode with a rounded plastic dome; the longer leg is positive (anode) and the shorter leg next to the flat rim is negative (cathode).
part_guide.res_220: A small beige cylinder with red-red-brown-gold color bands; it restricts current flow to protect the LED from burning out.
part_guide.pot1: A rotary dial with three metal legs; twisting the shaft adjusts the voltage output on its middle wiper pin.
part_guide.w_gnd_rail: A black jumper wire that brings ground (0V) from the Arduino GND pin to the top ground rail of the breadboard.
part_guide.w_led_sig: A yellow jumper wire that delivers the variable PWM output from digital pin 9 on the Arduino to the LED anode.
part_guide.w_led_gnd: A black jumper wire that runs straight up from the resistor to the top ground rail, closing the LED circuit.
part_guide.w_pot_5v: A red jumper wire carrying 5 volts of power from the Arduino to one outer pin of the potentiometer.
part_guide.w_pot_wiper: A blue jumper wire carrying the variable voltage from the potentiometer center pin to analog input pin A0 on the Arduino.
part_guide.w_pot_gnd: A black jumper wire connecting the other outer pin of the potentiometer directly to the top ground rail.

steps.title: Connect Arduino Ground to Breadboard Ground Rail
steps.instruction: Plug one end of a black jumper wire into the Arduino header pin labelled GND, and plug the other end into the first hole of the ground rail along the top edge of the breadboard (next to row 1).
steps.check: A black wire links the Arduino's GND header socket directly to the very first hole of the top outer rail.

steps.title: Insert the Yellow LED
steps.instruction: Insert the yellow LED into the breadboard: push the longer leg (anode, +) into row 10, column e (left half), and the shorter leg (cathode, -) into row 11, column e (left half).
steps.check: The yellow LED sits in column e spanning rows 10 and 11, with the longer lead in row 10.

steps.title: Insert the 220 Ohm Current-Limiting Resistor
steps.instruction: Insert one leg of the 220 ohm resistor (red-red-brown bands) into row 11, column d (left half), sharing the row with the LED shorter leg, and push the other leg into row 15, column d (left half).
steps.check: The 220 ohm resistor bridges column d between row 11 and row 15.

steps.check: A yellow wire runs from Arduino digital pin ~9 into hole a10 directly in line with the LED long leg.

steps.check: A black jumper wire runs straight upward from hole a15 to the top ground rail hole beside row 15.
